description.short: A local full-stack web app that turns AI-sourced job leads into a focused pipeline for reviewing roles, managing applications, and tracking outreach.
long: Agent tasks run research in the background, with progress, failures, and browser-access requests shown in the interface. Active tasks remain available across navigation and reloads, so reviewing a role or preparing an application doesn’t interrupt the research.

Job discovery and evaluation use separate agents, so the researcher gathering leads doesn’t also decide which ones qualify. Their handoffs preserve supporting evidence, with schema checks validating the results before they become saved job records.

Codex needs local access to Chrome, so I separated agent execution from the application’s data service. A Node bridge manages research tasks and browser permissions, while the API preserves job records and application history in PostgreSQL.

description.short: Tally is a cross-platform app for personal and shared counters on iOS, Android, and web, with real-time collaboration and offline synchronization.
long: Counting works offline as well as online, so updates happen locally before reaching the API. I used a persistent queue to retain pending changes through lost connections and app restarts.
A lost response can leave the client unsure whether an update was saved. Stable operation IDs let the server recognize retries and avoid applying the same increment twice.

Web and native clients share an authentication API, with HTTP-only cookies in the browser and secure device storage on native. When access tokens expire, concurrent requests share a single refresh request before retrying, with refresh-token rotation handled by the API.

description.short: A reaction-time training app with timed drills, animated feedback, user accounts, and performance history, backed by a secure Express/PostgreSQL API.
long: Animation carries the interface from setup through the countdown and into each round. GSAP timelines coordinate screen transitions with target and score feedback, including the shift from active play to the final result.

Each result keeps a snapshot of the settings used for that attempt. I carried that context into the profile’s filters, so results can be compared by their original target size and timing even after account preferences change.

The profile combines filtering and pagination with optional columns for saved settings. Its layout changes as those controls expand, so I used GSAP Flip to animate the reflow and adapted the controls for smaller screens.
